findings.title: Queries that interpolate to empty strings are not filtered out
findings.body: runSplitQuery filters targets on query.expr before calling applyTemplateVariables. If a target's raw expression is a non-empty variable that interpolates to an empty string, it is not discarded. It can then be grouped and sent to Loki as an empty query; if all targets become empty, the grouped requests array is empty and runSplitGroupedQueries can fail (Math.max over an empty array and undefined longest partition). Filter again after interpolation.

findings.title: Shard splitting now filters empty expressions before interpolation
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery changed from interpolating targets before filtering out empty expressions to filtering expressions first and interpolating afterwards. A query whose raw expr is a non-empty variable but whose interpolated expression is empty will no longer be discarded. This is a behavior regression and can create invalid shard queries or empty request groups. Add a filter after applyTemplateVariables.

findings.title: Already interpolated/sharded queries are interpolated again by runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates targets at the start and later calls runSplitQuery for each shard group. runSplitQuery now unconditionally interpolates targets again. The updated tests expect applyTemplateVariables to be called multiple times for one query in the shard flow. Because applyTemplateVariables receives request.filters and template replacement is not necessarily idempotent, repeated interpolation can duplicate ad-hoc filters or alter already-interpolated values containing '$'. This can change or corrupt the shard-modified query. Avoid re-interpolating already interpolated targets or make the operation explicitly idempotent.
